title: Latency attribution cohortboard: streaming vs blocking tail analysis
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a cohort-style dashboard ("cohortboard") that attributes tail latency (p95/p99) across model families and routes with an explicit split for streaming vs blocking (non-streaming) I/O. This ticket coordinates the telemetry changes, metrics pipeline aggregations, and dashboard panels so SREs and product teams can quickly identify whether tail regressions are due to model behavior, request shape, or serving path (streaming vs blocking). The dashboard should support filtering by model, route, region, and request-shape buckets (short/medium/long) and provide trace links to surface example traces for high-latency cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument metrics: all request spans emit io_mode tag (streaming|blocking), model_family, route, request_shape, token_count
Metrics pipeline: aggregated p50/p95/p99 by [model_family, route, io_mode, request_shape] available with 1m granularity
Dashboard: cohortboard with side-by-side streaming vs blocking panes, p50/p95/p99 sparklines, delta columns, and trace links to sample traces
Tracing hooks: trace ID injected into metric buckets so clicking a high-latency cell opens a trace sampler with representative traces
Performance: dashboard queries complete under 3s for 7d time window in staging
Runbook: short investigation playbook and alert thresholds documented in Confluence
telemetry_changes: Add field request.io_mode = streaming|blocking to request metrics and spans
Emit model_family label derived from model.catalog entry at routing time
Tag requests with request_shape (short|medium|long) computed from prompt token count thresholds
Add boolean span attribute 'kv_cache_hit' for primary caching layer
Include per-request route_version in metrics for rollout attribution
